name: The Tower of London (Her Majesty's Fortress)
description: Historic stone castle and royal fortress on the north bank of the River Thames, home to the Crown Jewels and 1,000 years of royal history.
history: Built by William the Conqueror to protect and dominate London; served as a royal residence, prison, armory, mint, and menagerie.
construction: Centered around the massive stone White Tower built with Caen limestone imported from Normandy.
architecture: Concentric fortress with inner and outer defensive curtain walls, water-gate (Traitors' Gate), and 21 towers.
currentStatus: Standing pristine in Central London, England.
